extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) handling reissue/correction matters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on correcting issued U.S. patents (reissue, certificates of correction, disclaimers), including statutory bases, filing content, timing (2‑year broadening rule), inventorship, priority/benefit claims, drawings, and examiner procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to correct patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be corrected or amended in eight ways, namely by: (1) reissue, (2) issuance of a certificate of correction which becomes part of the patent, (3) disclaimer, (4) reexamination, (5) supplemental examination, (6) inter partes review, (7) post grant review, and (8) covered business method review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first three ways are discussed in this chapter (reissue, certificate of correction, disclaimer). The other proceedings are discussed elsewhere (MPEP chapters cited). No new petitions for covered business method reviews after Sept. 16, 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for reissue (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue is available 'whenever any patent is, through error, deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid, by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than he had a right to claim in the patent.' No new matter shall be introduced into the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may issue several reissued patents for distinct parts upon demand and fee. Post-AIA law (effective Sept. 16, 2012) removed the 'without deceptive intention' clause; pre-AIA references are noted where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error must render patent wholly or partly inoperative/invalid (what counts as an error)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error for reissue purposes must be one that causes the patent to be deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid for the reasons specified in 35 U.S.C. 251; spelling, grammar, typographical, editorial or clerical errors that do not cause such inoperativeness are not grounds for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical/typo corrections may be made via a certificate of correction (see MPEP § 1481). Such non-substantive corrections may be included in a reissue application only if at least one 35 U.S.C. 251 error is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common bases for filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The most common bases are: (A) the claims are too narrow or too broad; (B) the disclosure contains inaccuracies; (C) applicant failed to or incorrectly claimed foreign priority; and (D) applicant failed to make reference to or incorrectly referenced prior copending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of these may support a reissue when they cause the patent to be partly or wholly inoperative/invalid under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter shall be introduced into the application for reissue; the reissue must be 'for the invention disclosed in the original patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue specification must contain the entire specification (including claims) and drawings of the patent as a copy of the printed patent; amendments are permitted only under the reissue amendment procedures and must preserve columnar format or be submitted as separate amendment papers with required markings (37 CFR 1.173).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening reissue two‑year rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No reissued patent shall be granted enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent (35 U.S.C. 251(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed within two years, diligence is presumed and examiners should not inquire why applicant failed to file earlier. Filing on the two‑year anniversary counts as within two years. See MPEP § 1412.03 for practice on broadening reissues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-of-claims error: omission of narrower claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission of a narrower claim from a patent can render a patent partly inoperative, permitting addition of narrower claims by reissue without narrowing preexisting patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue applicant can retain broad independent claims while adding new dependent (narrower) claims. However, failure to timely file a divisional after a restriction requirement is not considered an error correctable by reissue (see MPEP § 1412.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship errors — reissue vs certificate of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of misjoinder of inventors may be a ground for reissue; where correction of inventorship is the only change and parties agree, a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 256/37 CFR 1.324 may be issued instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventorship is contested or applicant chooses, inventorship may be corrected via reissue because misjoinder is an error correctable under 35 U.S.C. 251. See Ex parte Scudder and related authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority (foreign) and benefit claim errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue can be used to perfect or make a foreign priority claim or correct failures to claim benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or 35 U.S.C. 120, but may require petitions under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 depending on the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If priority claim was made but certified copy missing, reissue may perfect priority; where claim not made originally, reissue may be used but petitioner under 37 CFR 1.55(e)/(f)/(g) or 37 CFR 1.78(e)/(c) as appropriate is required showing good and sufficient cause or that delay was unintentional. In many cases a certificate of correction plus petition may be preferable (see MPEP § 216.01 and § 214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Error in drawings: substantive vs non‑substantive changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue may be based on a drawing correction that is substantive in nature (i.e., qualifies as an error under 35 U.S.C. 251); non‑substantive drawing changes (reference numeral corrections, shading additions, additional figure merely to clarify) do not by themselves provide a basis for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑substantive drawing changes may be included in a reissue application if at least one substantive 35 U.S.C. 251 error is being corrected. Drawings must be submitted as clean copies and changes made per 37 CFR 1.173(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in filing reissue applications (timing and courts' review)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is filed within 2 years from the date of the original patent, lack of diligence or delay rejections normally should not be made; courts, however, may scrutinize diligence (e.g., In re Rosuvastatin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not reject for lack of diligence for filings within two years, but be aware of case law where diligence for narrowing reissues was assessed by courts. Filing on cutoff dates and timing rules (37 CFR references) are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of papers where reissue patent is in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers for entry in reissue applications of patents involved in litigation should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the envelope and top right-hand portion of the papers and will receive special attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protestor participation is limited per 37 CFR 1.291(c); see MPEP §§ 1442.01–1442.04 for litigation-related reissue examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissue on patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue is for the unexpired part of the term of the original patent; reissue cannot extend the patent term. Deleting an earlier-obtained benefit claim (35 U.S.C. 120) via reissue will not lengthen the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reissue declaration indicates the correction is to extend term, examiner should point out statutory limits. Specific examiner actions differ if the deletion of benefit claim is the only error identified versus one of multiple errors (detailed handling described in § 1405 subsections A and B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and consideration of references cited in the original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: In reissue examination, the examiner should consider all references cited during original prosecution and list any reference again cited/applied on PTO-892. Applicant has a continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.56 to disclose material information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants wishing to ensure prior references are considered should file an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98. The Office no longer requires copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications in an IDS unless requested; legible copies required for foreign patents/publications and pending unpublished U.S. applications per 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2). If a previously-cited reference copy is unavailable except from applicant and not submitted, examiner will not consider it and will strike it from PTO/SB/08 listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of a reissue application (37 CFR 1.171, 1.173)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application must contain the same parts required for an original patent application and must furnish the entire specification, including the claims, and the drawings of the patent (copy of the printed patent in double column format), and comply with reissue rules; no new matter allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue oath/declaration complying with 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.175 is required. If the patent is assigned, a consent of assignee and evidence of ownership required; if unassigned, applicant should affirm patent is not assigned. Amendments at filing may be made by physically inserting changes into printed patent columns with markings or by separate amendment paper per 37 CFR 1.173(b). Retyped specifications allowed only with a grantable petition (37 CFR 1.183) when changes are extensive and reading is error-prone. Preliminary amendment cancelling all original claims without presenting new claims is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and marking requirements for reissue specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments at filing must follow 37 CFR 1.173(b)-(e) and (g); changes physically incorporated into printed patent must preserve columnar structure and use markings pursuant to 37 CFR 1.173(d) to show insertions/deletions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A caret and line to marginally inserted typed text may satisfy the 'typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink' requirement for additions. If changes are extensive, consider petition to submit a clean typed specification per 37 CFR 1.183.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date and missing parts in reissue application (37 CFR 1.53(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application can be accorded a filing date without an oath/declaration or without basic filing/search/examination fees being present; OPAP will accord a filing date and issue a missing parts notice providing time to supply missing parts and pay surcharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants given period to provide missing documents; surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) applies when filing incomplete. Note that 37 CFR 1.53(b) filing-without-claims provision does not apply to reissue applications because 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1) requires the entire specification including claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to prefer certificate of correction over reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical, typographical, spelling, grammar, or minor errors that do not cause the patent to be deemed inoperative/invalid should be corrected by a certificate of correction (35 U.S.C. 255), not by reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a priority/benefit claim can be corrected via certificate of correction plus appropriate petition (37 CFR 1.55/1.78), patentee should consider that route rather than reissue. Certificates of correction are limited to specified kinds of mistakes and corrections that do not add new matter or require reexamination (see In re Arnott).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling terminal disclaimers (pre- and post-issuance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recorded terminal disclaimer may be withdrawn before patent issuance or reexamination certificate issuance by petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or by refiling the application; after issuance, recorded terminal disclaimers generally cannot be nullified and reissue is not available to withdraw them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy disfavors restoring what was dedicated to the public; certificates of correction and reissue are limited in scope and cannot be used to nullify recorded terminal disclaimers after issuance. If a recorded terminal disclaimer contains errors in naming owners, patent owner may file explanatory papers and additional disclaimers to correct names for the file history; but substantive withdrawal after issuance is not addressed on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedural items and form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Office action in a reissue application should include form paragraph 14.01 (Reissue Application, Applicable Laws and Rules Heading). Various form paragraphs (e.g., 14.36.01) exist for examiner communications about refunds and terminal disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified form paragraphs to notify applicants about refund possibilities, terminal disclaimer forms on the USPTO website, and other standard examiner communications as noted in the MPEP. See examiner notes for specific paragraph usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in reissue proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has a continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.56 to timely apprise the Office of any information material to the patentability of the claims under consideration in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS in the reissue application is recommended to ensure original prosecution references are considered; failure to disclose material information may raise inequitable conduct or duty of disclosure issues addressed elsewhere in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of references not available except from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of a reference (other than U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication) cited in the original patent is not available and cannot be obtained except from the reissue applicant and the copy is not submitted, the examiner will not consider that reference and will not list it on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant listed such a reference on PTO/SB/08 but did not provide a copy, examiner will line-through the reference to indicate it was not considered. Applicants should submit copies or an IDS per 37 CFR 1.98 to ensure consideration.
